problem:
The depth $D,$ in meters, of a plant’s root system after $t$ months is modeled by $D(t)=\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{2t+13}.$ What is the instantaneous rate of change of the root depth when $t=6$ months?

The instantaneous rate of change when $t=6$ months is
{{field-1}} meters per month.
worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the root depth when $t=6$ months is equal to ${D}^{′}(6).$ 

First, we take the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{2t+13}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot (2t+13)^{(1/2)-1}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(2t+13)^{-1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $t=6,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{′}(6) & =\frac{1}{4}(2(6)+13)^{-1/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{25}} \\  & =\frac{1}{20}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change of the root depth when $t=6$ months is $\frac{1}{20}$ meters per month.
